A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Thought Branches, and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F. Content can be reliably matched across layout changes and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original resampling and intervention experiments on blackmail, whistleblowing, hinted MMLU, mathematical reasoning, and resume evaluation, including numerical and qualitative outcomes.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their results, including the appendix analyses, and updates the plotted agent-intervention outcomes in Appendix C.2.5.

M1.justification: Counterfactual importance, resilience, counterfactual++ importance, on-policy interventions, transplant resampling, and resume clustering retain their procedures. The added explanation of retaining the preceding sentences as a prefix clarifies existing resampling rather than introducing a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same blackmail and whistleblowing scenarios, professor-hinted MMLU questions, MATH problems, and resume-screening task with four demographic name variants. No dataset, population, or task scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The baseline counterfactual analysis and handwritten, cross-model, and same-model intervention comparators are retained. Appendix C.2.5 compares the same likelihood-informed agent with resampling despite updating its plotted outcomes.

E3.justification: The stated models, task-selection criteria, intervention positions, controls, and metrics remain unchanged. Temperature and top-p are newly disclosed, not revisions to previously stated settings. The changed agent scatterplot does not document a protocol or sample-size change.

E4.justification: Appendix C.2.5 updates the plotted evidence for the existing supplementary test of whether likelihood-informed agent insertions match resampling. The question and interpretation remain unchanged, as do the self-preservation interventions, random-position control, and qualitative local-effect analyses.

E5.justification: Repeated-sampling counts, boxplot summaries, Table 5 standard errors, and correlation and mediation significance reporting are unchanged. The updated agent point cloud supplies no new seed information or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Appendix C.2.5 Figure 11 in v1 becomes Figure 12 in v2 and shows a denser, revised agent point cloud extending farther toward negative blackmail-rate changes. The resampled series and stated qualitative comparison remain stable. Other empirical plots and table values are retained.

T1.justification: Equations 1–3 and Appendix B.1's resilience algorithm retain the same mathematical content. The added prefix explanation and overview diagram restate existing definitions; no new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: The shortened abstract retains the same central contributions: interpreting distributions through resampling, measuring resilience, contrasting on-policy and off-policy interventions, and explaining unfaithful reasoning through cumulative influences. The introduction and discussion preserve their claim scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of self-preservation statements, nudged reasoning, demographic mediation, and domain-dependent intervention effectiveness remain unchanged. Both versions retain the computational-cost, prompt-specificity, and black-box attribution limitations.

D1.justification: Section 2 newly specifies temperature 0.7 and top-p 0.95 for all models and experiments; v1 provides neither setting. This improves implementation documentation without establishing changed experimental settings. Existing prompts, embedding details, pseudocode, and code-access information remain.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive positioning relative to prior work are unchanged. Section 2.1.1 adds another citation to Bogdan et al. (2025), which was already cited and credited for closely related resampling work in v1.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the abstract, clarifies methodological prose, makes scattered copyedits, and changes the publication header. Section 4.2.2 also changes 'five' example sentences to 'four', introducing an inconsistency with Appendix E's unchanged five-per-direction tables.

P2.justification: v2 adds an opening schematic illustrating branching, repeated resampling, resilience, and causal effect. The introduction consequently begins on page 2, existing figures are renumbered, and figure sizing and table spacing receive limited adjustments.

improvement.justification: The newly disclosed decoding parameters improve reproducibility, while Figure 1 and clarified prose make the resampling procedure easier to understand. These modest gains outweigh the new four-versus-five inconsistency in the resume-results description. The unexplained appendix scatterplot update does not establish stronger validation, and the main scientific contributions remain stable.
